newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Berjaya shares down after requotation.
newsitem.headline: Berjaya shares down after requotation.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian property-based company Berjaya Industrial Bhd fell on Friday as trading in the stock resumed after a four-day suspension.
At 0828 GMT, the stock was trading at 1.90 ringgit, against its pre-suspension price of 1.98.
Berjaya Industrial earlier announced that it has acquired significant equity stakes in two Kuala Lumpur-listed companies for a total of 664.5 million ringgit.

It bought a 17 percent stake in maritime and engineering concern Promet Bhd for 350 million ringgit in cash and also a 32 percent stake in property and finance firm Kelanamas Industries Bhd for 314.5 million ringgit in cash.
Berjaya Industrial paid 3.50 ringgit for each Promet share and 8.50 ringgit for each Kelanamas share.
On Friday, Promet stock was trading at 2.14 ringgit and Kelanamas at 4.68 ringgit.
Berjaya Industrial is controlled by upcoming businessman Ling Hee Leong, son of Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik.
Promet and Kelanamas were previously controlled by businessman Soh Chee Wen.
